proposal._raw_text: {"weakness":"Warm batch latency is now ~45.8ms with cold ~45.9ms, so nearly all remaining time is fixed per-query work; no stage breakdown exists to show whether corpus normalization, hashing, or result assembly dominates, and RSS rose from 22016KB to 24588KB after the index change.","hypothesis":"A large share of the remaining ~45.8ms batch time is repeated per-query corpus normalization/tokenization work; reusing one hash-keyed parsed corpus per batch, guarded by corpus_sha256, should cut median and p95 batch latency by at least 20% without changing any per-query sha256 or counts.","metric":"median_batch_ms, p95_batch_ms, cold_batch_ms, rss_kb from the schema-1 benchmark; gate on correctness 1.0, zero failed_queries, and identical per-query sha256/count for all 20 queries versus corpus_sha256 37c5a6ee...","change":"Add stage timers around corpus load/normalize/score/assemble, then reuse a single parsed corpus per batch keyed by corpus_sha256, falling back to fresh parse on hash mismatch; keep result ordering and output bytes unchanged.","risk":"Cache keyed incorrectly or reused after mid-batch corpus mutation could return stale or wrong results, and retained parsed state could grow RSS further; mitigate by strict corpus_sha256 keying, hash-mismatch invalidation, and per-query sha256 equality checks.","reversible":true,"expected_files":["search/index.py","search/query.py","benchmarks/bench_search.py","tests/test_search_correctness.py"]}
proposal.change: Add stage timers around corpus load/normalize/score/assemble, then reuse a single parsed corpus per batch keyed by corpus_sha256, falling back to fresh parse on hash mismatch; keep result ordering and output bytes unchanged.
proposal.hypothesis: A large share of the remaining ~45.8ms batch time is repeated per-query corpus normalization/tokenization work; reusing one hash-keyed parsed corpus per batch, guarded by corpus_sha256, should cut median and p95 batch latency by at least 20% without changing any per-query sha256 or counts.
proposal.metric: median_batch_ms, p95_batch_ms, cold_batch_ms, rss_kb from the schema-1 benchmark; gate on correctness 1.0, zero failed_queries, and identical per-query sha256/count for all 20 queries versus corpus_sha256 37c5a6ee...
proposal.risk: Cache keyed incorrectly or reused after mid-batch corpus mutation could return stale or wrong results, and retained parsed state could grow RSS further; mitigate by strict corpus_sha256 keying, hash-mismatch invalidation, and per-query sha256 equality checks.
proposal.weakness: Warm batch latency is now ~45.8ms with cold ~45.9ms, so nearly all remaining time is fixed per-query work; no stage breakdown exists to show whether corpus normalization, hashing, or result assembly dominates, and RSS rose from 22016KB to 24588KB after the index change.
